claims: Sony's signed-zero table specifies a negative minimum when either zero operand is negative, and a negative maximum only when both zero operands are negative.

The proposed finite-input SQRT handling uses cause I bit 17, cause D bit 16 and sticky I bit 6, preserves negative zero, and returns the square root of the magnitude for a negative nonzero input; this does not establish general EE rounding equivalence.

Sony's conversion-overflow flag descriptions conflict: Table 8-4 reports no cause flag and CVT.W.S lists no flag assignments, while Table 8-6 reports I/SI set. The experiment leaves conversion flags unresolved.

evidence.text: Source https://docs.alexrp.com/mips/ee.pdf version6 printed159: I bit17, D16, O15,U14, SI6,SD5,SO4,SU3. Printed163 Table8-5: Max(+0,+0),Max(+0,-0),Max(-0,+0) result +0; Max(-0,-0) -0. Min(+0,+0) +0; other three min zero combinations -0. Printed162 Table8-4 conversion overflow cause None. Printed165 Table8-6 floating to integer overflow result 2^31-1 or -2^31, I(SI) set. Printed164: hardware rounding toward0 does not use guard,round,sticky bits and can differ from IEEE RTZ in least significant bit.

https://docs.alexrp.com/mips/ee_insns.pdf version6 printed356 CVT.W.S converts toward0, clamps when biased exponent>0x9d; no flag assignments in operation. Printed365 MIN clears O/U. Printed376 SQRT(-0)=-0; negative nonzero uses magnitude and sets I/SI, D=0.
